FortiGate workspace

The FortiGate ADOM works on a FortiGate live over the FortiOS REST API — the device's own measured GUI pages, which edit cmdb objects with a dry run first, an API console whose writes are dry-run by default, and 30 read-only section pages in the FortiOS menu's 7 areas.

🔑 Permissionsnetwork.view protection.view appliances.view appliances.edit network.edit registry.view registry.execute_write
📍 WhereProduct selector → FortiGate (URL /fgt/), section pages at /fgt/m/<item>

What is it?#

The FortiGate workspace is the SATOM ADOM for FortiGate firewalls. It shows a FortiGate's configuration live, in the layout of the device's own GUI, and reads everything from the FortiGate you selected: SATOM keeps no FortiGate configuration cache. SATOM 3.0 shipped it read-only; the measured GUI pages now edit cmdb objects (dry run first, read back and verified), and an API console sends cmdb writes, dry-run by default. The section pages stay read-only.

What does it do?#

  • Dashboard (/fgt/): the FortiGate devices you can see, with Select, the live Unit status of the selected unit (hostname, firmware, build, serial, model, log disk) and a map of every section.
  • The FortiGate menu in the sidebar: the pages of the unit's own GUI, drawn from the layout measured on its build (knowledge packs). All pages lists them in the device's menu order. These pages write: Create New, edit, Clone and Delete of a cmdb object, and the rows of its inline tables, as POST / PUT / DELETE on /api/v2/cmdb/<path>. Every save is a dry run first; the apply is audited and read back. Monitor views, GUI-only pages and fields measured with no API are drawn read-only and never saved. The menu ends with Not in GUI, but in CLI (see Not in GUI, but in CLI).
  • API → Registry & console: the FortiGate registry browsed as the FortiGate menu, and a live console. GET reads the cmdb, monitor and log trees; POST, PUT and DELETE go to /api/v2/cmdb/ only and are dry-run by default.
  • 30 section pages in 7 areas, following the FortiOS 8.0 menu, over 43 cmdb tables — one tab per table, read-only:
Area Sections
Network Interfaces (interfaces, zones), DNS, Routing (static and policy routes), SD-WAN, DHCP servers
Policy & Objects Firewall Policy, Addresses (IPv4, IPv6, groups), Services (custom, groups), Schedules, Virtual IPs, IP Pools, Traffic Shaping
Security Profiles AntiVirus, Web Filter, DNS Filter, Application Control, Intrusion Prevention, SSL/SSH Inspection
VPN IPsec Tunnels (phase 1, phase 2), SSL-VPN Settings
User & Authentication User Definition, User Groups, Authentication Servers (LDAP, RADIUS), Authentication Settings
System Settings (global, VDOM settings, NTP), Administrators (admins, REST API users, admin profiles), HA, SNMP, Certificates (local, CA)
Log & Report Log Settings (log settings, syslog)
  • The shared pages every ADOM offers — Appliances, Jobs, Notifications, Audit log, monitoring and metrics, Search, Architecture, Analysis, Change requests, Scheduled actions, API tokens — plus the Release notes window, Build compatibility and Schema builds.

Requirements#

  • A FortiGate reachable over HTTPS from SATOM.
  • A REST API administrator on the FortiGate and its token (execute api-user generate-key <api-user>). FortiOS 8.0 refuses password logins on the REST API. A read-only admin profile is enough to read everything. The token's profile also decides what a write may do: give it a read-write profile only if operators are to edit from SATOM.
  • A licensed FortiGate-VM: an unlicensed VM answers 401 to every REST call except its licence status.
  • SATOM's address in the API user's trusted hosts, if you restrict them.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the dashboard and the section pages Read access — any view permission, for example network.view
Open the FortiGate menu's pages protection.view
Apply a change on a FortiGate menu page Any key that grants configuration writes (legacy config_write), for example network.edit or appliances.edit
Open API → Registry & console, send GET registry.view
Send POST / PUT / DELETE from the console (dry run or apply) registry.execute_write
See the FortiGate in the appliance list appliances.view
Register or edit a FortiGate appliances.edit

Without a write key the menu pages open read-only: the dialog shows OK (Read-only: nothing is sent to the device.) instead of Save. Without registry.execute_write the console refuses a write method with The "Execute write API calls" permission is required for non-GET methods.

How to use#

Register a FortiGate#

  1. Switch to the FortiGate workspace and open Administrator → Appliances (without the administrator capability, Operations → Appliances).
  2. Add appliance: name, host, port (default 443), kind fortigate.
  3. In the password field paste the REST API token, not a login password. The username is informational (the API user's name).
  4. Optionally fill ADOM (vdom, optional) with the FortiGate VDOM: every read then carries ?vdom=<name>.
  5. Set TLS verification as for any appliance (import the FortiGate's CA under the trust store, or turn verification off for that device).
  6. For the SSH features (Diagnose Log Collection and Diagnostic Battery discovery), open the appliance's full edit page. Fill SSH user, if different from the API user and SSH password, if different from the API credential with a CLI administrator, because a REST api-user cannot open SSH.

Browse a FortiGate#

  1. On the dashboard, click Select on a FortiGate card (with exactly one FortiGate it is selected for you).
  2. Check the Unit status card: hostname, firmware and build confirm the token works.
  3. Open a page from the FortiGate menu in the sidebar, or a section from the dashboard map. A section whose every tab a measured page draws opens that page; any other section opens its read-only section page, where you switch tabs and expand raw on a row to see every field.

Change an object#

  1. Open the page from the FortiGate menu and open the object (or click Create New, or select a row and click Clone or Delete).
  2. Change the fields and click Save. SATOM shows Review the change: the exact request it would send. Nothing has been sent yet.
  3. Click Apply to <device>. SATOM sends the request, reads the object back from the FortiGate and compares it with what was sent. The save shows a badge: Verified on the device, Not applied (the value the unit kept, for example the device kept comment = 'old' (sent 'new'); the save fails) or Not verified (with the reason).

A save is accepted only for a collection the page itself edits. A field that is CLI-only on the unit's build goes through the CLI writer (see Not in GUI, but in CLI).

Send a call from the API console#

  1. Open API → Registry & console, pick the FortiGate, the method, a registry name (or a raw /api/v2/… path), an optional object key and a JSON body.
  2. A GET runs at once. A POST, PUT or DELETE returns the request it would send: Dry run — nothing was sent. Re-submit with Apply to perform this write on the device.
  3. Re-submit with Apply to send it. The reply is shown unchanged, with the verdict of a re-read beside it; the console reports, it does not fail.

There is no PATCH: FortiOS updates with PUT, and a PUT replaces a member list (srcaddr, member) instead of merging into it. See also Product API pages.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Kind fortigate Yes fortigate
Host / Port Management address and HTTPS port Yes 192.0.2.20 / 443
Username Informational: the REST API user's name No satom-ro
Password The REST API administrator token Yes (token)
ADOM (vdom, optional) The FortiGate VDOM to read No root

Example#

🧪Example — Changing an address comment

An operator selects fgt-edge-01 and opens the address page from the FortiGate menu. They open srv-web, change its comment and click Save. Review the change shows the PUT it would send to firewall/address. Apply to fgt-edge-01 sends it; the re-read finds the new comment and the save shows Verified on the device. No secret is ever displayed.

Result#

  • Reading changes nothing on the FortiGate or in SATOM. A section table shows at most 500 rows and says when it truncated. Secret fields (passwords, pre-shared keys, private keys) and every value FortiOS returns as ENC … are dropped before the page renders.
  • An applied change on a menu page is audited with a before-snapshot and a change-history row; a value the unit did not keep is audited as config.<action>.not_applied.
  • A console write is audited as fgt_api.execute with the method, the scrubbed body and the verdict.

Troubleshooting#

"401 unauthorized — the API token was refused, or the FortiGate-VM has no valid licence …"#

Possible causes - The password field holds a login password or an old token. - The FortiGate-VM is not licensed.

Solution 1. Generate a new key for the REST API user and store it as the appliance password. 2. License the VM.

Verification - The dashboard's Unit status shows hostname, firmware and build.

"403 forbidden — the token authenticated but its admin profile does not grant this resource, or the source address is not a trusted host."#

Possible causes - The API user's profile has no read access to that area. - SATOM's address is not in the API user's trusted hosts.

Solution 1. Grant read access to the area, or add SATOM as a trusted host.

"404 — no such resource on this firmware: …"#

Possible causes - The table does not exist on the FortiOS build the device runs.

Solution 1. Compare builds on Build compatibility.

"The device refused the status read."#

The dashboard's first read failed; the reason is printed under it (one of the errors above).

"The device answered successfully with zero objects — this is not an error."#

The table really is empty. On Administrators, a token whose profile is read-only is served no administrators at all: the empty list is the profile, not the device.

"No FortiGate is selected."#

Pick one on the dashboard (Pick a device).

"Not applied: the device kept …"#

Possible causes - The FortiGate accepted the write, but the re-read shows it holds another value than the one sent.

Solution 1. Read the value the unit kept, shown in the message. 2. Save again with a value the unit accepts, or make the change on the FortiGate itself.

Verification — the save shows Verified on the device.

"Writes go to /api/v2/cmdb/ only. …"#

The console refused a write to another tree: the monitor tree holds device actions (reboot, restore, firmware upgrade), not configuration. Nothing was sent.

"DELETE needs an object key: a DELETE on the whole table is refused, not sent."#

Name the object in the key field; a table-wide DELETE is never sent.

Advanced#

Advanced What is not there yet

Writes outside /api/v2/cmdb/ (the client refuses any other path, so no monitor action such as reboot, restore or firmware upgrade is ever sent), edits on the section pages, backups, restore, firmware, templates and Lua, HA status, threshold scopes, and the Migration report (it needs a stored show full-configuration dump, and no FortiGate backup is stored yet). SATOM edits one object at a time on one FortiGate; there are no fleet rollouts.

Advanced How FortiOS answers

Every answer carries version, build and serial, so the build is known from any call. An unknown table answers 400 — unlike FortiWeb, a 200 really means "served". A read-only profile reads each table, but the global schema index is 403. The FortiGate schema itself (CLI tree and per-table REST schema) reaches the API library through knowledge packs; this workspace does not harvest it.
